source: Macnamara & Maitra (2019) The role of deliberate practice in expert performance: revisiting Ericsson, Krampe & Tesch-Romer (1993)
finding: Double-blind replication of the original violin study. The core finding did not replicate: best violinists did not have more accumulated practice alone than good violinists. The effect was still substantial but smaller.
numbers: Accumulated practice alone to age 18: best M=8224 h, good M=9844 h, less accomplished M=4558 h. Best vs good t(24)=-0.93, p=.364, d=-0.38. Good vs less t=3.26, d=1.33. Group effect eta2=.26 (CI .03-.44). About 13 per group (N=39). Original had 3 groups of 10.
quote: We did not replicate the core finding that accumulated amounts of deliberate practice corresponded to each skill level.
limits: Violin only, student sample, retrospective estimates.
agent_relevance: Practice volume stops separating the top from the next tier. Do not assume more rounds always separates best from good.

source: Macnamara & Maitra (2019) replication: teacher-designed vs solitary practice
finding: Teacher-designed practice (the theoretical definition) explained no more variance than practice alone (the operational definition). Best violinists reported LESS weekly practice than good ones.
numbers: Teacher-designed practice to age 18: best 6251 h, good 6821 h, less 2799 h; eta2=.23 (CI .02-.41) vs .26 for practice alone; r=.72 between the two. Current weekly practice alone: best 22.69 h vs good 30.65 h, p=.024, d=-1.03. Estimates exceeded diary logs, F(1,35)=19.62, eta_p2=.36, with the same bias across groups.
limits: Small N. Ericsson (2014) reported a 95% CI of 2894-11926 h for the original best group, which already contained the good-group mean of 5301 h.
agent_relevance: The label 'deliberate practice' is unstable. Any practice step in a scaffold needs an operational definition.

source: Hambrick, Macnamara & Oswald (2020) Is the Deliberate Practice View Defensible? A Review of Evidence and Discussion of Issues
finding: Review of 25+ years of Ericsson's writings. The definition shifted (who designs the activity, whether a teacher is needed). The authors say this makes the view hard to falsify. Meta-analyses give 14% to 37% of variance explained depending on domain and coding.
quote: Does deliberate practice leave more of the variance in performance unexplained than it explained?
limits: Authors are the critics, so this is partly advocacy.
agent_relevance: A fair summary: practice explains a third at most; other factors explain the rest.

source: Hambrick, Altmann, Oswald, Meinz & Gobet (2014) Facing facts about deliberate practice
finding: Reply to Platz et al. A music r of .61 still leaves room for two other predictors of similar size. Retrospective estimates may be inflated if people recall practice from their skill.
numbers: Their chess plus music meta-analysis: DP accounted for about one third of reliable variance in each domain (about 30% in music). r=.61 leaves room for two orthogonal predictors of r=.56 each.
quote: deliberate practice accounted for about one-third of the reliable variance in performance in each domain
limits: Reply paper, not new data. Platz's .61 could be a lower or an upper bound.
agent_relevance: Retrospective self-report is weak. Prefer logged practice, as in the 2026 Chess.com study.

source: Platz, Kopiez, Lehmann & Wolf (2014) The influence of deliberate practice on musical achievement: a meta-analysis
finding: First music-only meta-analysis. Practice is strongly linked to achievement; authors argue r, not r2, should be reported.
numbers: 13 studies, total N=788, corrected r=.61, 95% CI [.54, .67].
limits: Broad definition (any task-specific accumulated practice). Music only.
agent_relevance: Upper end of the estimates; effect size depends on domain and measure.

source: Gobet & Ereku (2014) Checkmate to deliberate practice: the case of Magnus Carlsen
finding: Case test of the monotonic assumption: the world number one had fewer years of serious practice than the next ten players.
numbers: Carlsen 18 years since starting age vs mean 24.6 years for ranks 2-11; t(9)=2.83, p<.05, difference 6.6 years (CI 1.33-11.87). Rating 2881 vs next ten M=2780.6, t(9)=-19.38. Rank vs years r=-0.21, p=.55. Win probability vs peers 63.7%.
limits: Starting age is a crude proxy for practice. N=11. No hours measured. One outlier case.
agent_relevance: Differences at the frontier are not explained by volume. Quality and talent-like factors matter.

source: Mosing, Verweij, Hambrick, Pedersen & Ullen (2024) Testing the Deliberate Practice Theory: does practice reduce the heritability of musical expertise?
finding: Twin test of a clean DP prediction: genetic influence should shrink with practice. It did not shrink. Relative heritability rose.
numbers: 6471 twins, 1302 complete pairs. About 50% genetic, 25% shared environment, 25% residual. More practice cut shared-environment and residual variance; genetic variance stayed constant.
quote: genetic predisposition remains important for musical expertise even after prolonged practice
limits: Music, auditory discrimination as the expertise measure, self-reported lifetime hours. Shared-environment decrease not significant.
agent_relevance: The sharpest test against a pure-practice theory. Do not assume more practice washes out baseline capacity.

source: Macnamara, Moreau & Hambrick (2016) The Relationship Between Deliberate Practice and Performance in Sports: A Meta-Analysis
finding: Sports: DP explains 18% overall but only 1% among elite athletes. Earlier starting age did not separate higher from lower skill.
numbers: Overall 18% of variance; elite-level performers 1%.
limits: Abstract only. Range restriction at the elite level is a rival explanation for the 1%.
agent_relevance: Skill level moderates: returns to practice volume shrink at the top.

source: Gobet & Campitelli (2007) The role of domain-specific practice, handedness, and starting age in chess
finding: Chess practice correlates with rating but with huge individual variation. Practice is necessary but not sufficient.
numbers: N=104 in the abstract (Hambrick 2020 says 90 members). r=.42 between DP hours and rating. Hours to reach master ranged 3016 to 23608 (about 8-fold). Starting age correlated with skill.
quote: The slower player needed 8 times as much practice to reach master level than the faster player.
limits: Abstract plus citing text only; N differs between sources. Retrospective questionnaire, one Argentine club sample.
agent_relevance: Show variance, not only the mean, when reporting how much practice is needed.

source: de Bruin, Smits, Rikers & Schmidt (2008) Deliberate practice predicts performance over time in adolescent chess players and drop-outs
finding: Longitudinal mixed model of young Dutch elite players: serious solitary study and serious play predicted rating, equally for persisters and drop-outs.
numbers: Abstract only; no coefficients read. Drop-outs developed more slowly but gained the same per unit of practice. Gender effect much smaller than practice effect.
limits: Abstract only. Better players may practise more (confounding).
agent_relevance: Supports a within-person dose-response; weaker for between-person explanation.

source: Vaci, Edelsbrunner, Stern, Neubauer, Bilalic & Grabner (2019) The joint influence of intelligence and practice on skill development throughout the life span
finding: Longitudinal chess study. Intelligence and practice both raise skill, with a nonlinear interaction: more intelligent players gain more per unit of practice, peak higher and decline less.
numbers: Abstract only; no numbers read.
quote: more intelligent individuals benefited more from practice
limits: Abstract only.
agent_relevance: Gain from a practice loop depends on a learner capacity. Efficiency differs by learner, not only by loop.

source: Southwick, Harwell, Wright, Olsen & Ogles (2026) Not All Practice Is Created Equal: Longitudinal Evidence From Over 40,000 Chess Players
finding: Large logged-data study. Deliberate-practice-aligned activities gave much greater rating gain per hour than playing games, though over 90% of time went to games.
numbers: N=44,213 Chess.com players, objective timestamped logs, multilevel models. 3.61x learning efficiency for DP-aligned activity vs gameplay, ps<.001. Not all DP activities equally effective.
quote: despite more than 90% of player time being spent on games, deliberate practice was substantially more efficient for learning
limits: Abstract only read. Author team includes Ericsson's collaborator Harwell. Observational: players choose activities. Measures rating gain per time, not variance explained.
agent_relevance: Best direct evidence that practice TYPE matters. For an agent: targeted drills beat replaying whole tasks.

source: Li, Tang, Yang & Tang (2023) Deliberate practice and clinical competence of residents: systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs
finding: Randomised trials: DP beats traditional teaching on checklist scores but not on a global rating scale.
numbers: 10 RCTs, 277 residents. Checklist (182 residents): MD=4.44, 95% CI 1.72 to 7.15, p=.001. OSATS global rating (66 residents): MD=1.34, CI -2.82 to 5.51, p=.53.
limits: Abstract only. Small trials, mixed scales, loss to follow-up.
agent_relevance: Experimental evidence that structured practice with feedback raises checklist-type skill.

source: Clark, Harwell, Ericsson & Boot (2022) Applying aspects of deliberate practice to help low performers improve manual control in a complex task
finding: Space Fortress experiment. A 90-min intervention (video demos plus continuous auditory feedback) helped initially low performers more than undirected training. Gains held after feedback was removed.
numbers: Abstract only; no effect size read. After 4 h of gameplay the intervention group beat the undirected group on manual control.
limits: Abstract only. Low performers only, short horizon.
agent_relevance: Short, targeted, feedback-rich practice can beat plain repetition. This is an interventional result, not a correlation.

source: Song (2026) Deliberate practice in the age of artificial intelligence: AI-assisted practice, self-regulated learning and expert performance in conservatory musicians
finding: Three-wave observational study. AI practice tools linked to later self-regulated learning, which linked to later instructor-rated performance.
numbers: 16 weeks, 512 of 600 musicians finished (85.3%). AI practice T1 to SRL T2 beta=.47; SRL T2 to performance T3 beta=.39; indirect effect=.183 (95% CI .124-.251); direct path beta=.14. CFI=.96, RMSEA=.045.
quote: These coefficients are interpreted as longitudinal associations rather than causal effects.
limits: Observational, self-reported predictors, mixed apps, not randomised. Author says associations, not causal.
agent_relevance: Weak AI-era evidence. Treat as a hypothesis: AI feedback may work through learner self-regulation.

source: Zhang, Han, Li, Chen & Lin (2025) Complete Chess Games Enable LLM Become A Chess Master (ChessLLM)
finding: Plain supervised fine-tuning on full games turns an LLM into a chess player. Data design (long vs short rounds) changes strength a lot.
numbers: Elo 1788 vs Stockfish with 10 samples. Long-round supervision gave +350 Elo over short-round data.
limits: Only the abstract page was read. Elo is computed against Stockfish levels, not a standard rating. Best-of-10 sampling inflates it. The 2026 critic (b18) reports 99.11% legal moves and 1530 Elo under a different calculation.
agent_relevance: Training on whole trajectories rather than fragments is the nearest LLM analogue to practice at the right grain. It changes weights, not a scaffold.

source: Wen, Tang & Anderson (2025) ChessQA: Evaluating Large Language Models for Chess Understanding
finding: Benchmark in five levels that follow the learner path (Structural, Motifs, Short Tactics, Position Judgment, Semantic). Current LLMs show persistent weaknesses in all five.
numbers: No per-model scores on the abstract page. 33 pages, 8 figures.
limits: Numbers not read; full paper not opened.
agent_relevance: A curriculum-shaped benchmark could drive the diagnostic half of deliberate practice (find the weak skill, then drill it).

source: Tang (2026) Generalization or Memorization? Brittleness Testing for Chess-Trained Language Models
finding: A 25M-parameter model trained only on puzzle positions beats larger chess LLMs on puzzles, but one trained only on self-play positions fails. The author argues puzzle scores reflect pattern matching.
numbers: Mate-in-N (n=300 in tables; methods say 600): KinGPT-Woodpecker 71.9% puzzle accuracy, Chimera 74.5%, Beaver (54,681 self-play positions) 2.1%. ChessGPT-Base 16.1% normal, 38.6% pass@10. KinGPT-Chimera 70.3% vs C1-4B 53.6% first-move accuracy over 20 themes. Stockfish 18 Level 0: 63.7%.
quote: impressive benchmark scores of chess-trained language models are largely explained by pattern-matching
limits: Single-author preprint. n mismatch noted. Wide 99% Wilson intervals.
agent_relevance: Narrow drill on one distribution transfers badly to another. Supports checking transfer, not only drill scores.

source: Tang (2026) brittleness paper: verifier loop (LLM-Modulo) results
finding: A critic loop (returns legal moves, rejects non-improving moves, resets after 3 parse failures) lifts a weak general model but hurts a chess-tuned one at pass@10.
numbers: RedPajama 3B: legal-move sanity 50.8% (pass@10) to 95.3% (modulo); position accuracy 2.0% to 21.2%; puzzle accuracy 1.4% to 10.9%. ChessGPT-Base: puzzle accuracy 38.6% (pass@10) fell to 18.7% (modulo). OpenLLaMa 3B modulo: 3.7% puzzle, 12.1% position.
limits: Small models only; modulo uses K=10 with critics.
agent_relevance: Feedback helps most when the base model is weak. Do not add a critic to a strong solver without testing.

source: Miller et al. (2019) reanalysis, as reported in Hambrick 2020
finding: Rival meta-analysis found r=.40, almost equal to .38, but coded studies the original authors did not call deliberate practice (for example a chess study that said it did not interpret its measure as DP).
numbers: Miller 2019 k=70, r=.40 (CI .34-.46), 16.0%. Ericsson & Harwell 2019 coded 8 DP effect sizes and 6 purposeful-practice ones; r=.56, 31.4%. Macnamara 2014 r=.38.
limits: Secondhand, from critics. Both sides argue about coding.
agent_relevance: The number is stable across coders (about .4). The fight is about meaning.

source: Hambrick et al. (2020): Ericsson's inclusion standards
finding: Claim of inconsistent standards: Ericsson (2014) rejected a music study for range restriction, then Ericsson & Harwell (2019) coded one such study as DP.
numbers: Gobet & Campitelli 2007 chess: r=.42 (about 18% variance), 3016 to 23608 h to reach master.
limits: Critic's account of the opponent; read replies before relying.
agent_relevance: Inclusion rules matter as much as sample size.

source: Hambrick et al. (2020): Charness et al. (2005) chess dispute
finding: Charness 2005 chess was called 'the most compelling and detailed evidence' for designed training by Ericsson, but Moxley et al. (2019) later described it as evidence for 'purposeful practice'.
numbers: Charness 2005: Study 1 N=239; Study 2 N=169; earlier 1996 chapter N=136.
limits: Terminology shifted between citing papers.
agent_relevance: The same chess data was cited under two labels, so counts of DP studies are not independent evidence.

source: Hambrick et al. (2020): the uncontroversial claims
finding: Authors accept two points: expertise needs gradual training, and training can raise skill a great deal (Ericsson 1980: a student trained over 200 h on digit span). The dispute is about between-person differences.
numbers: More than 200 h of training lifted one college student's digit span (Ericsson 1980).
limits: Narrow skill, single-subject style evidence.
agent_relevance: Practice works within a person on a narrow task. It is a different question from who ends up best.

source: Macnamara, Hambrick & Oswald (2014) meta-analysis, read via Hambrick 2020 text
finding: Original large meta-analysis. DP explained 14% of variance overall. Games 24%, music 23%, sports 20%, education 5%, professions 1%.
numbers: 88 studies in the variance analysis (157 effect sizes). A corrigendum was published in 2018.
limits: Read only via the 2020 review. Corrigendum not read. Self-report and logs are pooled.
agent_relevance: Games (chess) are among the domains with the largest practice effect, about a quarter of variance, so chess is a high-ceiling case for DP.

source: Hambrick et al. (2020): reliability-corrected variance
finding: If measures were only acceptably reliable (.60), DP could explain up to 40% of variance; if excellent (.90), 18%. The unexplained share stays at least as large as the explained share except under low-reliability assumptions.
limits: Corrections depend on assumed reliability; 100% is not credible and shows the limit of the method.
agent_relevance: Measurement reliability limits every conclusion in this field.
